title: Has Oklahoma Ever Beaten Notre Dame? OU's Two Wins, 1956 and 2013
question: How many times has Oklahoma beaten Notre Dame in football?
answer: Oklahoma has beaten Notre Dame twice in 11 meetings: 40-0 in South Bend on October 27, 1956, and 35-21 in South Bend on September 28, 2013. Notre Dame won the other nine games on the field, though its 2012 win was later vacated by the NCAA.
summary: OU has beaten Notre Dame only twice: 40-0 in South Bend in 1956 and 35-21 there in 2013. Here's the story of both wins in a series the Irish dominate.
body: Notre Dame has been one of the few programs to consistently get the better of Oklahoma. Across 11 meetings, the Sooners have won just twice, and both victories came on the road in South Bend.

The first was a statement. On October 27, 1956, second-ranked Oklahoma, then 4-0 and in the middle of Bud Wilkinson's famous winning streak, visited Notre Dame Stadium and won 40-0 in front of 60,128 fans. OU led 26-0 at halftime and scored in every quarter. It is still cited as the worst home loss in Notre Dame history. The Irish got a measure of revenge the next year, but the 1956 rout remains one of the most lopsided results in the series.

Oklahoma then went 57 years without beating the Irish, losing seven straight meetings. That changed on September 28, 2013. The 14th-ranked Sooners jumped to a 14-0 lead after two quick interceptions of Tommy Rees, including a 24-yard touchdown return by linebacker Corey Nelson. Quarterback Blake Bell completed 22 of 30 passes for 232 yards and two touchdowns, hitting Sterling Shepard for a 54-yard score in the fourth quarter as OU won 35-21.

That 2013 game was the back half of a home-and-home that began with a 30-13 Notre Dame win in Norman in 2012, and it is the most recent meeting between the programs. The 2012 result is one of the Notre Dame wins from its 2012 and 2013 seasons that the NCAA later ordered vacated, which is why some series records show an asterisk.
So the answer for trivia night: two wins, 1956 and 2013, both in South Bend.
